text: The Reputation Stadium Tour was Taylor Swift's fifth concert tour and her first all-stadium tour, supporting her 2017 studio album *Reputation*. It began on May 8, 2018, in Glendale, Arizona, and concluded on November 21, 2018, in Tokyo, Japan, spanning 53 shows across 7 countries. The set list primarily featured songs from *Reputation* and included tracks from her other albums, with the stage design emphasizing snake motifs reflecting both the album's concept and Swift's public image. The main stage resembled a skyscraper under construction with a wedge-shaped display and featured elaborate lighting, while two smaller B-stages were used for acoustic "surprise song" performances. The October 6, 2018, show at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, was recorded and released as a Netflix original concert film on December 31, 2018, which was removed from Netflix on December 30, 2023. Music critics praised the tour for its Gothic visuals, Broadway theatricality, stage design, production, and wardrobe, highlighting Swift's showmanship and intimate connection with the audience. The tour attracted 2.88 million attendees and grossed $345.6 million, becoming the highest-grossing US and North American tour upon completion, and won Tour of the Year at the People's Choice Awards, American Music Awards, and iHeartRadio Music Awards. Swift launched the *Reputation* promotional cycle with the release of the lead single "Look What You Made Me Do" on August 24, 2017, and partnered with Ticketmaster for a "Verified Fan" program called "Taylor Swift Tix" to combat bots and scalpers, allowing fans to gain pre-sale access through activities like purchasing music or streaming videos. *Reputation* was released on November 10, 2017, selling over one million copies in the US and two million worldwide in its first week. On November 13, 2017, Swift announced 27 US dates for the tour; tickets went on sale to the public on December 13. On November 27, she announced three UK dates, followed by nine additional dates—three UK, five US, and one Canada—due to overwhelming demand. On December 3, five Australasia dates were added. In January 2018, due to high demand, Swift added second dates in Santa Clara, Landover, Philadelphia, Minneapolis, and Arlington, and third dates in East Rutherford and Foxborough, bringing the North American leg to 40 shows. On March 1, 2018, Camila Cabello and Charli XCX were officially announced as opening acts; Cabello had been previously speculated and promoted via a sweepstake at Live 95.5. On May 7, 2018, Swift invited 2,000 foster and adopted children to a private dress rehearsal; the following day, she announced two Tokyo shows in partnership with Fujifilm Instax, with Charli XCX as the opening act. In September, Broods was announced as an opening act for the Oceania leg. During the tour, Swift performed surprise songs from her back catalog at various venues, with a streaming-exclusive compilation, *Reputation Stadium Tour Surprise Song Playlist*, released on November 30, 2018, and certified triple platinum in Brazil. Media outlets gave the tour rave reviews, calling it one of the best of 2018, praising Swift's on-stage persona, seamless transitions, production value, wardrobe, and intimate moments. Stereogum's Chris DeVille described it as a "hyper-maximalist" tour, a "perpetual gargantuan flex," and a "roving musical Infinity War," calling it an "oversized, high-tech touring Broadway production" and placing Swift in the same rarefied tier as classic rock deities. Rob Sheffield of Rolling Stone called it Swift's "most astounding tour yet," noting its "mass communion" vibe and highlighting the powerful acoustic performances of deep cuts. The Guardian's Bob Gordon praised the opener "Ready for It?" as a "striking entrance," while Roisin O'Connor of The Independent compared the tour to a Broadway show due to its red lighting and trapeze dancers. Lydia Burgham of The Spinoff described the Auckland concert as a "theatrical, mega-production that somehow also strips down to raw intimate moments," noting Swift's ability to connect with fans through acoustic guitar and piano performances. Variety's Chris Willman noted the show's fierceness and the presence of "the guileless Swift," commending Swift for creating a holistic performance and highlighting the acoustic version of "Dancing with Our Hands Tied" as proof that *Reputation* worked acoustically. Randy Lewis of the Los Angeles Times praised Swift's use of modern technology, including light-up bracelets that made fans feel like participants, and noted the stage's resemblance to a skyscraper in progress with six crane-like structures. Greg Krelenstein of V magazine stated Swift had a rare gift of turning a stadium spectacle into an intimate setting, praising her command of the stage and her musical evolution. Ed Masley of The Arizona Republic noted moments when Swift performed directly to the back rows, while Jim Harrington of The Mercury News affirmed her improved vocal and performance skills. Chris Tuite of CBS San Francisco emphasized the prominent, vicious-looking snakes throughout the set. Michael Tritsch of 303 magazine called the tour a "breakthrough" that "set the bar high for future stadium tours." After four days of Verified Fan sales and three days of public sales beginning December 13, the tour had grossed $180 million from 33 North American dates. Pollstar reported that at least 35,000 tickets were sold at ten stadiums, with the highest at Lincoln Financial Field (48,039) and Heinz Field (35,419), and the May 12, 2018, show at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara generated nearly $9 million, prompting an extra date. The tour is the best-selling female tour in the UK in 2018. The first seven shows grossed $54 million with 390,000 tickets sold, placing Swift at the top of Billboard's Hot Tours chart in June 2018. She performed to sold-out crowds of 59,157 in Glendale and 107,550 in Santa Clara (over two nights), grossing $7.21 million and $14 million respectively, with Pasadena earning nearly $16.3 million and Seattle over $8.6 million. Louisville and Columbus concerts grossed $11.5 million with around 115,000 tickets sold, with Columbus having the highest gross and ticket sales at approximately 63,000 and $6.6 million, leading her back to the top of the Hot Tours chart. The tour broke multiple venue attendance and grossing records: the Glendale opening show set new gross and attendance records, surpassing Metallica's 2017 gross by nearly $2 million and breaking One Direction's attendance record by 2,633 seats; the Levi's Stadium show grossed $14 million from 107,550 tickets, surpassing her own 1989 World Tour records; the Rose Bowl two-show run earned $16.2 million, surpassing U2's 2017 record by over $467,000; at CenturyLink Field, she topped U2's 2017 gross by $2.4 million; and at Sports Authority Field at Mile High, she surpassed the 2011 record by $1.2 million. Swift became the first female artist to headline Dublin's Croke Park twice, with 136,000 fans in attendance, and the first woman to headline three consecutive nights at MetLife Stadium and Gillette Stadium. After the 29th North American show at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami, the tour had grossed $202.3 million in North America ($191.1 million in the US and $11.1 million in Canada), breaking her own record for the highest-grossing North American tour by a female artist. The tour eventually surpassed the Rolling Stones' *A Bigger Bang Tour* to become the highest-grossing tour in US and North American history, grossing $266.1 million—beating the Stones' $245 million from 70 shows—while Swift achieved this with only 38 shows. It also holds the Guinness World Record for the highest-grossing tour by a female artist in 2018. Minnesota Governor Mark Dayton declared August 31, 2018, as "Taylor Swift Day" in honor of her two shows at United States Bank Stadium, citing her music's inspiration and influence on truthfulness, grace, philanthropy, and strength. The concert film documenting the second performance at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, was released on December 31, 2018, exclusively via Netflix and was filmed on the last day of the North American leg. Tamlyn Wright and Baz Halpin were nominated for "Variety, Reality or Event Special" at the 24th Art Directors Guild Annual Excellence in Production Design Awards for their work. The film received widespread critical acclaim, with critics calling it "immortalizing" and "unforgettable," praising the camerawork and Swift's stardom and emotional connection with the crowd. Rob Sheffield of Rolling Stone stated the film "immortalizes her best tour yet" and shows the "stadium-rocking spectacle without toning down any of her songs' one-on-one emotional intimacy." Amanda Petrusich of The New Yorker described it as "the end of an era," suggesting it will be remembered as a museum piece or a testament to Swift's era-defining longevity. Denis Warner of Billboard noted the film illuminates Swift's power, dedication, and strength as an artist, allowing a deeper understanding of her performance and staging. Benjamin Smith of Decider called it an "intimate document of an impersonal event," stating Swift is the only early 21st-century pop queen who has turned her music into something more than mere pop. Nardin Saad of the Los Angeles Times praised Swift's connection with her fans.

The Netflix special on Taylor Swift's performance has been described as "the end of an era" by Amanda Petrusich of The New Yorker, who noted it will likely be seen either as a museum piece or as a testament to Swift's era-defying longevity. Billboard's Denis Warner praised the film for illuminating Swift's power, dedication, and strength as an artist, highlighting how it offers a deeper understanding of her as a performer and the delicate staging of the event, while appreciating Swift for providing a gorgeous look into her world as one of today's greatest entertainers. Decider's Benjamin Smith called the film an "intimate document of an impersonal event" and asserted that Swift will stand the test of time more than her fellow early 21st century pop queens, citing that she is perhaps the only one who has figured out a way to turn her music into something more than mere pop. Nardin Saad of the Los Angeles Times commended Swift's star power, stating it is "tantamount as evidenced" in the film. Katie Collins of CNET observed that the film serves as a reminder that Swift's stardom is perennial, praising the costumes, dancing, and Swift's own barely-contained effervescent joy on stage, while noting that closeups brought new insights into the show. Nicholas Hautman of Us Weekly appreciated the camerawork for capturing fans hysterically crying and screaming in support of their idol. Chloe Gilke of Uproxx labeled the film a "masterful documentation of the magical energy at a pop show" and a "love letter to the audience at her shows, and to her fans," emphasizing that it honors the sacred joy of Swift's performance that night and the people who made it happen, and lauded the camerawork for capturing the massive scope of the production from every angle and the audio, which is crystal-clear and beautiful, with the crowd quieted down so viewers at home can hear Swift best.
